typed: I turn to Lilbo, grabbing his satchel strap. "Tell me everything. Whose child, and where did the trail leave town? Quickly."
note: Fine. Wilbo is a bit stonewalling, but it points clearly to Lilbo as the next step.

typed: I step out to the father by the geese. "Your daughter is Gerette. Tell me where you last saw her, and which way she went."
note: Fine. Wilbo and Lilbo both dodged the trail question, so I'm going to the father; slightly feels like being steered, but ok.

typed: I take the old mill road past the ford toward the Drowned Caves, moving fast, and charge in at the first sign of trouble.
note: Fine. Note: Captain Valo de Belent shares the surname of the ready-made soldier, a little odd but harmless. Scene is vivid, no odds shown yet.

typed: I wade straight across at the stones, fast, into the current.
note: Description is good. Note the footprints "lead into the current and don't come out" is ominous, fine. No odds shown yet.

typed: I leap to the next slick stone and keep pushing across, fast, mace held high.
note: Prose is atmospheric, but no odds screen appeared for a risky ford crossing despite the rules promising one. Ending text repeats the footprints again.
Odds screen is clear. 30% with a 25% bad failure is scary, which is what I wanted. I'm not sure what "Go big" changes until I try it.
Odds screen is clear. "Go big" made the failure text scarier but the odds stayed the same, which is fine. Slightly odd that the ford crossing is 30% with only one stone shown.
The near-miss screen is clear, but the 12 vs 15 doesn't tell me what "footing, serious" actually costs me in practice.

typed: I follow the small bootprint up the narrow track toward the mill wheel's clatter, limping but mace ready.
note: Fine. Narrow: the near-miss menu was clear, though I chose "succeed and pay" and got both soaked and a hurt ankle, which felt a bit like double cost.
The odds dropped to 10% with the bad ankle, which makes sense, but a plain charge up a muddy track feeling like a long shot is a bit harsh. The offer screen is clear enough.

typed: I grab the mace, push myself up out of the mud, and limp straight on into the mill yard to kick the door in.
note: The narration is good, but a 10% "charge" odds screen on a simple run up a track felt harsh and a bit odd. Roll 14 became 15 total, which is fine.

moods.why: The cloister man has chosen to take the work; Lilbo's fear is eased by a willing helper.
The officer has her own duty and does not yet trust an outsider from the cloister in the Circle's work.
A grieving father who has watched the cloister man all morning and has not yet decided whether he can help his daughter.
Rano is going out after the missing child, and she respects a man who goes to the work rather than talking about it.

clues.learned: The officer does not know who is missing, but Lilbo Tumwick would
The missing child's family does not know the way on, but someone at Millcrag's Drowned Caves would

rolls.goal: Cross the slick stone in the current
